items.text: There was a man of Hawaii. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was poor but brave. <break time="0.8s" /> And who could read and write. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a schoolmaster. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a sailor. <break time="0.8s" /> And one day. <break time="0.8s" /> His ship took him to San Francisco. <break time="0.8s" /> A great city on the coast of America. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking up a hill in the city. <break time="0.8s" /> He stopped in front of a small but beautiful house. <break time="0.8s" /> With bright windows. <break time="0.8s" /> At one of the windows. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood an old man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who looked out at Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> With a face full of sadness. <break time="0.8s" /> What a fine house this is thought Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> If I lived in a house like that I would laugh all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man invited him inside. <break time="0.8s" /> And brought out a round bellied bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> With a long neck. <break time="0.8s" /> Made of glass as white as milk. <break time="0.8s" /> An imp lives in this bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the old man. <break time="0.8s" /> And Keawe saw something move inside it. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a shadow and a fire. <break time="0.8s" /> It was this very bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That had made Napoleon. <break time="0.8s" /> The king of the world. <break time="0.8s" /> But you must sell it. <break time="0.8s" /> For less than you paid. <break time="0.8s" /> And if you die with it. <break time="0.8s" /> You will burn in the fire forever. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man had paid ninety dollars for it. <break time="0.8s" /> And he sold it to Keawe for fifty. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was exactly all the money. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe had.

There was a man of Hawaii named Keawe, who was poor but brave, and who could read and write like a schoolmaster. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a sailor, and one day his ship took him to San Francisco, a great city on the coast of America. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking up a hill in the city, he stopped in front of a small but beautiful house with bright windows. <break time="0.8s" /> At one of the windows stood an old man, who looked out at Keawe with a face full of sadness. <break time="0.8s" /> What a fine house this is, thought Keawe, If I lived in a house like that, I would laugh all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man invited him inside and brought out a round bellied bottle with a long neck, made of glass as white as milk. <break time="0.8s" /> An imp lives in this bottle, said the old man, and Keawe saw something move inside it like a shadow and a fire. <break time="0.8s" /> It was this very bottle, he said, that had made Napoleon the king of the world. <break time="0.8s" /> But you must sell it for less than you paid, and if you die with it, you will burn in the fire forever. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man had paid ninety dollars for it, and he sold it to Keawe for fifty, which was exactly all the money Keawe had.

하와이에 한 남자가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨라는 이름의. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 가난했지만 용감했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 글을 읽고 쓸 줄 알았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 학교 선생님처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 선원이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 어느 날. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 배가 그를 샌프란시스코로 데려갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳은 미국 해안의 큰 도시였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 도시의 언덕을 걸어 올라가다가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 앞에 멈춰 섰다 작지만 아름다운 집. <break time="0.8s" /> 창문이 환한. <break time="0.8s" /> 창문 하나에. <break time="0.8s" /> 한 노인이 서 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 케아웨를 내다보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 슬픔이 가득한 얼굴로. <break time="0.8s" /> 정말 멋진 집이구나 케아웨는 생각했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 저런 집에 산다면 하루 종일 웃을 텐데. <break time="0.8s" /> 노인은 그를 안으로 들였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 배가 둥근 병을 꺼내 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 목이 긴. <break time="0.8s" /> 우유처럼 하얀 유리로 만든. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 병 속에는 작은 악마가 산다오. <break time="0.8s" /> 노인이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 케아웨는 그 안에서 무언가가 움직이는 것을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그림자처럼, 불꽃처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 이 병이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 말로는. <break time="0.8s" /> 나폴레옹을 만든 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 세상의 왕으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 반드시 팔아야 하오. <break time="0.8s" /> 산 값보다 싸게. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 병을 가진 채 죽으면. <break time="0.8s" /> 영원히 불길 속에서 타게 될 거요. <break time="0.8s" /> 노인은 그 병을 90달러에 샀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그는 케아웨에게 50달러에 팔았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 정확히 돈 전부였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨가 가진.

Keawe did not believe the story. <break time="0.8s" /> At first. <break time="0.8s" /> So he spoke to the bottle and said. <break time="0.8s" /> I want my fifty dollars back. <break time="0.8s" /> At once his pocket felt heavy again. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he counted the money. <break time="0.8s" /> He found exactly fifty dollars there. <break time="0.8s" /> Next he sold the bottle to a shop. <break time="0.8s" /> For sixty dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> But it did come back. <break time="0.8s" /> For that night. <break time="0.8s" /> It lay in his sea chest. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe told everything. <break time="0.8s" /> To his friend Lopaka, a fellow sailor. <break time="0.8s" /> Who advised him. <break time="0.8s" /> To go home and wish for something good. <break time="0.8s" /> Back in Hawaii. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe heard sad news. <break time="0.8s" /> For his uncle had died. <break time="0.8s" /> And his uncles son had drowned at sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Their land and money. <break time="0.8s" /> Now belonged to Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was exactly the amount. <break time="0.8s" /> That his dream house would cost. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon a grand house. <break time="0.8s" /> With three floors. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood on the mountainside. <break time="0.8s" /> And people called it the Bright House. <break time="0.8s" /> Lopaka wanted to buy the bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> But first he asked to see the imp. <break time="0.8s" /> And when it came out. <break time="0.8s" /> Both men froze with fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Even so. <break time="0.8s" /> Lopaka bought it. <break time="0.8s" /> Because he dreamed of having a ship of his own. <break time="0.8s" /> And he left that very night. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe slept well. <break time="0.8s" /> For the first time in days. <break time="0.8s" /> Glad that the bottle was no longer his.

Keawe did not believe the story at first, so he spoke to the bottle and said, I want my fifty dollars back. <break time="0.8s" /> At once his pocket felt heavy again, and when he counted the money, he found exactly fifty dollars there. <break time="0.8s" /> Next he sold the bottle to a shop for sixty dollars, but it did come back, for that night it lay in his sea chest. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe told everything to his friend Lopaka, a fellow sailor, who advised him to go home and wish for something good. <break time="0.8s" /> Back in Hawaii, Keawe heard sad news, for his uncle had died and his uncles son had drowned at sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Their land and money now belonged to Keawe, and it was exactly the amount that his dream house would cost. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon a grand house with three floors stood on the mountainside, and people called it the Bright House. <break time="0.8s" /> Lopaka wanted to buy the bottle, but first he asked to see the imp, and when it came out, both men froze with fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Even so, Lopaka bought it, because he dreamed of having a ship of his own, and he left that very night. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe slept well for the first time in days, glad that the bottle was no longer his.

케아웨는 그 이야기를 믿지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 처음에는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 병에 대고 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 내 50달러를 돌려받고 싶어. <break time="0.8s" /> 곧바로 그의 주머니가 다시 묵직해졌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 돈을 세어 보니. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에 정확히 50달러가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 다음으로 그는 병을 가게에 팔았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 60달러에. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 병은 정말로 돌아왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 왜냐하면 그날 밤. <break time="0.8s" /> 병이 그의 선원 상자 안에 놓여 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 모든 것을 털어놓았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 동료 선원인 친구 로파카에게. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 케아웨에게 권했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 고향에 가서 좋은 것을 빌어 보라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 하와이로 돌아오자. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 슬픈 소식을 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 삼촌이 세상을 떠났고. <break time="0.8s" /> 삼촌의 아들은 바다에서 물에 빠져 죽었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들의 땅과 돈은. <break time="0.8s" /> 이제 케아웨의 것이 되었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그것은 정확히 그 금액이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 꿈꾸던 집을 짓는 데 드는. <break time="0.8s" /> 곧 웅장한 집이. <break time="0.8s" /> 3층짜리. <break time="0.8s" /> 산비탈에 섰다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 사람들은 그 집을 빛나는 집이라고 불렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 로파카는 병을 사고 싶어 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 먼저 그는 악마를 보여 달라고 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 악마가 나오자. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 사람 모두 두려움에 얼어붙었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런데도. <break time="0.8s" /> 로파카는 그것을 샀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 왜냐하면 그는 꿈꾸었기 때문이다 자기 배를 갖는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그는 바로 그날 밤 떠났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 푹 잤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 며칠 만에 처음으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 기뻤다 병이 더 이상 자기 것이 아니라서.

One evening. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe met a beautiful young woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Kokua by the road. <break time="0.8s" /> And before they parted. <break time="0.8s" /> She agreed to marry him. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe rode home singing with joy. <break time="0.8s" /> But that night. <break time="0.8s" /> As he got ready for his bath. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw a strange spot on his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the Chinese Evil. <break time="0.8s" /> A terrible sickness. <break time="0.8s" /> For which there was no cure. <break time="0.8s" /> In those days. <break time="0.8s" /> People with this sickness. <break time="0.8s" /> Had to leave their families. <break time="0.8s" /> And live apart. <break time="0.8s" /> On the island of Molokai. <break time="0.8s" /> If I had not sold the bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> I could have wished this sickness away. <break time="0.8s" /> Thought Keawe with a heavy heart. <break time="0.8s" /> It was not the house but Kokua. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could not give up. <break time="0.8s" /> So he decided. <break time="0.8s" /> To find the bottle again. <break time="0.8s" /> He sailed to Honolulu. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he learned that Lopaka had sold it. <break time="0.8s" /> And that it had passed from hand to hand. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he found it with a young man. <break time="0.8s" /> In Beritania Street. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had paid only two cents for it. <break time="0.8s" /> I am sorry for you. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the young man. <break time="0.8s" /> For one cent is the smallest coin. <break time="0.8s" /> And you can never sell it again. <break time="0.8s" /> Still Keawe bought it for one cent. <break time="0.8s" /> And the moment he made his wish. <break time="0.8s" /> His skin became clean and healthy.

One evening Keawe met a beautiful young woman named Kokua by the road, and before they parted, she agreed to marry him. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe rode home singing with joy, but that night, as he got ready for his bath, he saw a strange spot on his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the Chinese Evil, a terrible sickness for which there was no cure in those days. <break time="0.8s" /> People with this sickness had to leave their families and live apart on the island of Molokai. <break time="0.8s" /> If I had not sold the bottle, I could have wished this sickness away, thought Keawe with a heavy heart. <break time="0.8s" /> It was not the house but Kokua that he could not give up, so he decided to find the bottle again. <break time="0.8s" /> He sailed to Honolulu, where he learned that Lopaka had sold it and that it had passed from hand to hand. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he found it with a young man in Beritania Street, who had paid only two cents for it. <break time="0.8s" /> I am sorry for you, said the young man, for one cent is the smallest coin, and you can never sell it again. <break time="0.8s" /> Still, Keawe bought it for one cent, and the moment he made his wish, his skin became clean and healthy.

어느 저녁. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 아름다운 젊은 여인을 만났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 길가에서 코쿠아라는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그들이 헤어지기 전에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 그와 결혼하기로 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 기뻐서 노래하며 말을 타고 집에 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 그날 밤. <break time="0.8s" /> 목욕할 준비를 하다가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 피부에 이상한 반점을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 중국병이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 무서운 병. <break time="0.8s" /> 고칠 방법이 없는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 시절에는. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 병에 걸린 사람들은. <break time="0.8s" /> 가족을 떠나야 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 따로 떨어져 살아야 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 몰로카이섬에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 병을 팔지 않았더라면. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 병이 사라지게 빌 수 있었을 텐데. <break time="0.8s" /> 케아웨는 무거운 마음으로 생각했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 집이 아니라 코쿠아였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 포기할 수 없는 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 결심했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 병을 다시 찾기로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 호놀룰루로 배를 타고 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서 그는 알게 되었다 로파카가 병을 팔았다는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 병이 이 사람 저 사람 손을 거쳐 갔다는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 마침내 그는 한 젊은이에게서 병을 찾았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 베리타니아 거리의. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 병을 겨우 2센트에 샀었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 안됐군요. <break time="0.8s" /> 젊은이가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 1센트는 가장 작은 동전이니까요. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 당신은 다시는 팔 수 없어요. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래도 케아웨는 1센트에 병을 샀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 소원을 빌자마자. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 피부는 깨끗하고 건강해졌다.
